doc.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

title: First solo in second grade, 'My Red Robin'
summary: Zottola recognizes the tune as his second-grade solo, where he froze on the bridge and his mother's pep talk got him back on stage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I’ve got a story for you on that. “My Red Robin.” That’s “My Red Robin.” That is my first solo that I played in second grade. Here’s the story, in front of the entire school my mother played like Count Basie, she was my accompanist. So I played that tune in second grade and I was nervous and I went blank on the bridge. And I ran off stage crying. And then my mother came to me and gave me a pep talk and I came back on and finished it to a standing ovation. And it goes to show you a little encouragement early on goes a long way.
You know I thought about that because —
Why did you pick that tune?
Well because — no I read it.
Oh. Okay. I said this guy’s clairvoyant.

It struck a nerve with me because when I was in fourth grade I was playing the flutephone, which is like a recorder. And I did pretty well and my tune was “The Marine’s Hymn.” So, but not quite as sophisticated as — I mean that “Red Red Robin” has a [scats] it’s like a tricky bridge for a second grader.
Well they played it on jazz gigs in the old days, you know, yeah.
